input: Turning to the absorber itself, the wall thickness adopted for the absorber is 20 mm, a figure that is arrived at once the corrosion allowance has been added on top of the thickness that is required by the pressure considerations alone. The allowance is applied in full on the process side of the wall, which is the side that is exposed to the circulating solvent, since it is there that the wastage of the metal is expected to take place over the life of the vessel. As far as the gasket materials for the flanged joints of the absorber are concerned, the two candidate materials have been compared with one another purely on the basis of their temperature limits, and it is on that basis that a preference emerges. Other considerations, such as the behaviour of the materials under the bolting loads and their general availability, have deliberately been set to one side for the purposes of this particular comparison, because it is the temperature limit that separates the two materials by a margin that is significant in the context of this service. The material with the higher temperature rating is the one that is preferred, since its limit sits comfortably further above the temperatures that the joint will experience in service, and this additional margin is obtained without the need for any change to the flange facing or to the bolting that is used.
target: The wall thickness adopted for the absorber is 20 mm, after the corrosion allowance is added to the thickness the pressure duty requires. The allowance is carried in full on the process side, the side wetted by the solvent the lean solvent pump keeps in circulation, because that is the surface from which metal is lost in service. For the gasket at the absorber flanges, the comparison of the two candidate materials is made on temperature limit only. Seating behaviour, resistance to the solvent, and availability are excluded from this comparison, not because they do not matter, but because the temperature limit is the property on which the two materials differ by a margin that bears on the duty. The higher-rated material is preferred. Its limit stands further above the highest temperature the joint can reach, including the excursions that follow a loss of circulation, and the margin is gained without any change to the flange facing or the bolting. The lower-rated material stays within its limit in normal operation, but with a margin that an excursion consumes, and the same comparison, on the same basis, remains open at the discharge flange of the lean solvent pump.
